resources.string: Enable the Vikey keyboard in Settings
Settings › System › Languages & input › On-screen keyboard › turn on Vikey.
Choose Vikey as the current keyboard
Tap here, choose Vikey with the keyboard switcher, then type
Type an English word while in Vietnamese (or the other way round): Vikey fixes that word and switches modes. Press delete right after to undo.
After you press the VI/EN key yourself, Vikey doesn\'t auto switch for 5 seconds, so your choice sticks.
In a web address, email or web search field, Vikey starts in English and returns to the previous language when you leave the field.
Where the tone mark goes with oa, oe, uy: new style (hoà, thuý) or old style (hòa, thúy).
Only add marks when the word being typed follows Vietnamese spelling rules.
When a finished word isn\'t valid Vietnamese, Vikey puts back exactly the keys you typed.
Show suggested words above the keyboard, Vietnamese and English. Tap one to use it.
When you hit the key next to the one you meant ("teh" instead of "the"), Vikey fixes the word when you press space. Press delete right after to keep what you typed.
The first letter of a sentence is capitalized, like the system keyboard.
A light tick on every key, like the system keyboard.
Double-tap the space bar to insert a period followed by a space.

Above the keys, show how long each tap takes to process, how many vibrations and touches, and write it to a log. The log never contains what you type, only timings and key kinds (letter, space, delete…).
Nothing yet. Open the Vikey keyboard and type.
Vikey is designed and developed by Tony Dinh, based on the open-source OpenKey project by Tuyen Mai. Open source under the GPL-3.0 license.
Type English in the middle of a Vietnamese sentence: Vikey fixes it and switches modes for you.
Switch to Vikey with the keyboard icon on the navigation bar
The keyboard never connects to the internet. What you type doesn\'t leave the device.
Tap the box below, choose Vikey with the keyboard switcher, then type "tooi ddi meeting nhes".
Vikey switches languages using word statistics counted from these sources. The app contains only the statistics, no text.
Used only to measure and improve accuracy; not included in the app.
